 Key points
 Level 3 basic pay is ₹21,700 at the entry cell of the 7th CPC pay matrix. 
 Dearness Allowance rises from 60% to 63% of basic pay with effect from 1 July 2026, making DA ₹13,671 a month on the Level 3 entry basic. 
 House Rent Allowance is a percentage of basic pay only, depending on whether the city is X, Y or Z class. 
 Gross pay totals ₹47,749 in an X-class city, ₹45,579 in Y-class cities on the higher Transport Allowance list such as Lucknow or Jaipur, ₹42,645 in other Y-class cities and ₹40,475 in a Z-class city. 
 Advertisement
 A central government employee at the entry cell of Level 3 draws basic pay of ₹21,700, which with DA, HRA and Transport Allowance works out to ₹47,749 a month gross in Delhi.
 The starting point is basic pay itself. Under the Central Civil Services (Revised Pay) Rules, 2016, “‘pay in the Level’ means pay drawn in the appropriate Cell of the Level as specified in Part A of the Schedule” — for Level 3, that entry cell is ₹21,700. The Level itself corresponds to the pre-2016 grade pay or scale of the post. Level 3 has 40 cells in all, so basic pay rises with each annual increment: ₹21,700 at the first cell, ₹24,500 at the fifth, ₹28,400 at the tenth and ₹69,100 at the fortieth.
 The Department of Expenditure’s office memorandum dated 29 October 2026 raises Dearness Allowance (DA), the inflation top-up on basic pay, from 60% to 63% of basic pay with effect from 1 July 2026. On the Level 3 entry basic of ₹21,700 that comes to ₹13,671 a month.
 House Rent Allowance (HRA) is worked out “of Basic Pay only” — no other allowance is added into the figure HRA is calculated on. The percentage depends on the city’s classification: on the rates in force, 30% in X-class cities, 20% in Y-class cities and 10% in Z-class cities, with floors of ₹5,400, ₹3,600 and ₹1,800. The classification annexure to the office memorandum of 7 July 2017 lists “Delhi (UA)” among the eight X-class cities, with Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Greater Mumbai, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Pune. On ₹21,700 basic, HRA is ₹6,510 in an X-class city, ₹4,340 in a Y-class city and ₹2,170 in a Z-class city.
 The Department of Expenditure’s Transport Allowance order fixes the allowance for Level 3 at ₹3,600 a month in the cities on its own list and ₹1,800 elsewhere, with DA paid on it as well — ₹5,868 and ₹2,934 in all. The list has every X-class city, and Y-class cities such as Lucknow, Jaipur, Kanpur, Surat, Nagpur, Indore and Patna.
 Adding these together, gross pay at the Level 3 entry cell comes to ₹45,579 a month in a Y-class city on the higher Transport Allowance list, such as Lucknow or Jaipur. It is ₹42,645 in other Y-class cities and ₹40,475 in a Z-class city. This is gross pay: NPS, CGHS, CGEGIS and any income tax are cut from it. Work out the figure for a different cell or Level with the 7th/8th CPC pay matrix .
 These pay rules cover central civil services and posts paid from the Civil Estimates, and the Indian Audit and Accounts Department. Railway employees and defence civilians are paid under their own ministries’ rules, which use the same pay levels.
 These documents do not give the rate for the next DA revision, due from 1 January 2027.
 Source: Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure — DA O.M. No. 1/2(i)/2026-E.II(B) (effective 01.07.2026); Central Civil Services (Revised Pay) Rules, 2016, Gazette notification of 25 July 2016; HRA O.M. No. 2/5/2017-E.II(B) of 7 July 2017; Transport Allowance O.M. of 7 July 2017.

 Critical AdSense behaviour: adsbygoogle.push({}) does NOT bind to
 a specific . It says "process the next unbound in DOM
 order." So if you push N times, AdSense binds the first N 
 slots it finds.
 Live investigation (2026-05-29) showed the right sidebar still
 loading late on indianpaycalculator.in. DOM order of :
 1. LEFT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-left)
 2-5. Display banners (4× AdBanner inside page content)
 6. RIGHT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-right, after main slot)
 7. Mobile anchor (StickyAnchorAd at body end)
 Previously this script pushed twice (one per sidebar). Those 2
 pushes bound LEFT + Display#1, NOT LEFT + RIGHT. The other 5
 slots only got bound as AdBanner.client:visible islands hydrated
 on scroll — meaning the right sidebar was bound 6th, after the
 user scrolled past every in-page banner. That's the "right side
 opens very late" complaint.
 Fix: push once per SSR'd ad slot. AdSense binds them all in DOM
 order at body parse end — no React hydration wait, no scroll-to-
 view wait. Subsequent React useEffect pushes (from AdUnit /
 StickyAnchorAd) become no-ops since the AdUnit effect skips when
 data-adsbygoogle-status is already set. --> component was removed 2026-05-29 to eliminate the
